headline: Zimbabwe thumps Bangladesh by an innings and 85 runs in Harare
summary: Zimbabwe secures their biggest-ever Test victory as Bangladesh collapses in their second innings on Day 3.
details: Zimbabwe registered their biggest victory in Test cricket by defeating Bangladesh by an innings and 85 runs on Tuesday in Harare.
Resuming their second innings at 40 for one, Bangladesh was bowled out for 185 in 45 overs, lasting just over a session.
Blessing Muzarabani led the attack with 4 for 65, while Richard Ngarava and Newman Nyamhuri picked up three and two wickets respectively.
Najmul Hossain Shanto (30) and Mushfiqur Rahim (34) provided the only significant resistance with a 61-run partnership.
Other batters including Mahmudul Hasan Joy (22) and Amite Hasan (25) failed to make a significant impact as the team slumped to an innings defeat.
The match ended on Day 3, with Bangladesh failing to replicate the first-innings application shown by Mominul Haque.
caption:
Zimbabwe's biggest Test win ever! 🏏
Bangladesh suffers an embarrassing innings defeat in Harare.

Zimbabwe registered their biggest victory in Test cricket by defeating Bangladesh by an innings and 85 runs on Tuesday in Harare.

Resuming their second innings at 40 for one, Bangladesh was bowled out for 185 in 45 overs, lasting just over a session.

Blessing Muzarabani led the attack with 4 for 65, while Richard Ngarava and Newman Nyamhuri picked up three and two wickets respectively.

Najmul Hossain Shanto (30) and Mushfiqur Rahim (34) provided the only significant resistance with a 61-run partnership.

Other batters including Mahmudul Hasan Joy (22) and Amite Hasan (25) failed to make a significant impact as the team slumped to an innings defeat.

The match ended on Day 3, with Bangladesh failing to replicate the first-innings application shown by Mominul Haque.

Of these total deaths, 93 children have died specifically from confirmed cases of measles.

In the last 24 hours, 980 children were affected by measles or measles-like symptoms, with 114 confirmed cases of measles and 866 showing symptoms.

Over the past 3.5 months, a total of 113,042 children have been affected by measles or measles-like symptoms.

The two most recent deaths occurred in Dhaka and Sylhet.

Since March 15 of this year, 101,177 children have shown symptoms of measles, and 11,965 have been confirmed as having measles.

During this period, 84,627 children were admitted to hospitals, and 80,974 have since been discharged after recovering.

In the last 24 hours, 821 children were admitted to hospitals for measles and measles-like symptoms.
